tasks.short: Work out cost of pallets, packaging, fuel, agency hours and overhead from quotes, rate cards and price lists.

today.trigger: A supplier quote, a new agency rate card, a price-list change or a cost-centre owner asking what something will cost.
steps: Open the quote or price list (PDF or Excel from Outlook or the agency portal)
Copy prices and quantities into an Excel cost sheet
Add overhead mark-ups per site from last year's allocation key
Check against last purchase prices in AFAS
Send the result to the requester or file it in SharePoint
drudgery: Looking up last purchase prices by hand
Rebuilding the same overhead formula each time
today.time_sinks: Retyping quote lines and hunting old prices in AFAS take most of the time; the arithmetic itself is quick.

lenses.faster: A model call reads the quote or rate card into a fixed cost template, prices are checked against AFAS purchase history and the overhead key is applied by formula; the bookkeeper reviews flagged differences in about 10 minutes instead of 30–40.
lenses.autonomous: A quote arriving in the AP mailbox or an agency portal rate change starts extraction and comparison; the sheet is ready without the bookkeeper and they approve it before it goes to the requester.
lenses.ambitious: Price every agency order line against the CAO-based rate card before the hours come in, so Operations sees the cost of a flex shift when ordering; demand for this would grow as it gets cheaper because planners order flex workers weekly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping PDF prices; bookkeepers want more time on spotting suppliers that quietly raise prices.
lenses.options: Two or three supplier quotes side by side with total cost including overhead and payment terms change which supplier gets the order, not just the effort.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper keeps the price and rate-card master data and the overhead key per site, and signs off which price deviations get flagged to purchasing; slightly more expert.
reach: Take over cost-per-shift comparisons from the FP&A Analyst, learning the site allocation model
Check agency rate cards against CAO wage scales with the Payroll Specialist, learning the CAO pay tables

tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a quote leaves out transport, waste or CAO allowances, and asking the supplier or site manager the right question before a number is trusted.
tasks.pattern_why: Quotes and rate cards arrive as varied PDFs; one model call turns them into a fixed cost template, after which lookups and overhead are plain formulas.

in_practice.trigger: New quote or rate card lands in the AP mailbox or agency portal
steps: Model extracts supplier, items, units and prices into the cost template
Template looks up last AFAS purchase price and flags changes above a set tolerance
Overhead key per site applied by formula
Bookkeeper reviews flags and sends the cost sheet
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves the cost sheet before it is shared or used for an order.
data_needed: AFAS purchase history per item and supplier
CAO wage tables for agency rates
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint cost-sheet library with source document and reviewer name

evidence.claim: Coding and line suggestions from vendor history that a team reviews and confirms cut per-invoice handling from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds in one vendor case.
AFAS Profit reads PDF documents to line level and fills supplier data; gaps are filled by hand.
LLM extraction of tables from varied PDF quotes into a fixed template is reliable enough for review-based use.

risks: Extraction misreads units (per pallet vs per piece) and the cost is off by a factor
Overhead key goes stale and every sheet inherits the error
Requesters treat the sheet as a final budget commitment
research_questions: How many quotes and rate cards a month reach Finance, and how many are in a format the model reads cleanly?
How often do last-purchase-price checks in AFAS actually catch a price increase today?
Do the three agencies publish rate cards in a stable format, or does each change it per season?

tasks.short: Match Rabobank statement lines to open invoices in AFAS and chase what does not match.

today.trigger: Daily CAMT.053 bank statement import from Rabobank into AFAS.
steps: Import the statement into AFAS
Let AFAS auto-match and review the proposals
Search open items by hand for unmatched lines
Book bank costs, interest and unclear receipts to suspense
Email customers or colleagues about unknown payments
drudgery: Searching for customers who pay several invoices in one amount without reference
Booking the same bank charges every day
Keeping a suspense list in Excel
today.time_sinks: Lines without a usable reference: combined payments, partial payments and agency or customer remittances that need a remittance advice from email.

lenses.faster: Tuned AFAS match rules (reference, IBAN, invoice number, tolerance) plus fixed rules for bank charges clear most lines; a model call proposes a match and a reason for the rest from remittance emails, so daily work drops from about 20 minutes to under 8.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly CAMT.053 import starts matching; rules post exact matches without the bookkeeper and only unmatched or tolerance-hit lines land in a queue with a suggested match.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile daily on all three sites' accounts and give the Credit and Collections Officer a same-morning list of who paid, so dunning stops for customers who already paid; demand grows if cheaper because collections calls depend on it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses booking bank charges or scrolling open-item lists; bookkeepers would rather sort out the odd customer who keeps paying without reference.
lenses.options: Little; there is one right match, so multiple drafts do not change the decision.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns match rules and tolerances in AFAS, decides which payment types post automatically, and reviews a short exception queue each morning; more expert in AFAS setup.
reach: Take over cash-position reporting from the Controller's month-end checklist, learning cash forecasting basics
Feed paid/unpaid status to the Credit and Collections Officer daily, learning the dunning process

tasks.human_edge: Recognising a misdirected or suspicious payment, and contacting the customer when a remittance makes no sense.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS matches on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount by written rules; the model only explains leftovers.

steps: AFAS auto-match posts lines that hit reference, IBAN, invoice number or oldest-first sum rules
Fixed rules book bank charges and interest
Model reads remittance emails and suggests matches for unmatched lines
Bookkeeper clears the exception queue
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every suggested match outside the rules and any posting to suspense.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank-statement booking log with matching rule or reviewer

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number, then oldest-first sums, exact unless a tolerance is set; misses go to a person.
Let AP run with people on exceptions and log every decision with its data.

risks: Too-loose tolerance books a payment to the wrong customer
Remittance emails contain personal data and must stay within AVG-compliant systems
Suspense items pile up if the queue is not owned daily
research_questions: What share of Noordhaven's bank lines does AFAS auto-match today, and with which rules switched on?
Which customers cause most unmatched lines, and would a payment-reference request fix them?
How long do items sit in suspense at month end?

tasks.short: Build AP and AR ageing, cash receipts and cost overviews for the controller and site managers.

today.trigger: Weekly AP/AR review, month close, or a request from the Controller or a site manager.
steps: Export open items and ledger data from AFAS
Clean and pivot in Excel
Add comments on large or old items
Send the file by email or put it on SharePoint
drudgery: Same export and pivot every week
Checking the Excel against Power BI when numbers differ
today.time_sinks: Re-exporting and reformatting the same data, and explaining differences between the Excel and the nightly Power BI refresh.

lenses.faster: Standard ageing, cash-receipt and DSO pages are built once in Power BI on the AFAS extract; a model call drafts the commentary on top items, so a weekly hour becomes 15 minutes of checking comments.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh updates the reports; on Monday a draft commentary on overdue and unusual items is ready for the bookkeeper to edit before it goes out.
lenses.ambitious: Give each of the three site managers a weekly view of their own open supplier invoices and overdue customers for the first time, so they chase approvals and disputes themselves; demand would grow if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the weekly export-and-pivot; bookkeepers want to spend the time explaining why an item is old.
lenses.options: Little; the numbers are fixed, only the commentary varies.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper decides which items get flagged and annotated and owns report definitions with the People Analytics/HRIS and finance BI owner; more analytical.
reach: Take over the DSO and ageing slide for the Controller's month pack, learning how the Controller reads it
Maintain Power BI finance pages with the FP&A Analyst, learning basic Power BI modelling

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the story behind an old item (a dispute, a credit note on its way, a customer in trouble) and saying it plainly to the reader.
tasks.pattern_why: Report definitions are fixed and run on the AFAS extract; only the commentary needs a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly Power BI refresh; weekly schedule
steps: Power BI refreshes ageing, cash receipts and DSO pages
Rules flag items above amount or age thresholds
Model drafts one-line comments from AFAS notes and email threads
Bookkeeper edits and publishes
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves commentary before it is sent.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI report history and SharePoint pack folder

evidence.claim: Scheduled BI reports on an ERP extract replace manual export-and-pivot for recurring finance reports.

risks: Nightly extract lags, readers act on yesterday's numbers
Generated comments sound sure about disputes the model only guessed
Site managers see customer data they should not
research_questions: Which recurring reports do the three bookkeepers produce, and how many hours a month each?
Does the current Power BI AFAS extract hold open-item detail at invoice level?
Who reads the weekly ageing, and what do they do with it?

tasks.short: Run the trial balance in AFAS at month end and clear odd balances before the controller reviews.

steps: Run the trial balance in AFAS
Export to Excel and compare with last month and budget
Look up odd balances and suspense accounts
Book corrections or pass them to the Accountant
Hand the checked trial balance to the Controller
drudgery: Tracing the same recurring differences every month
today.time_sinks: Hunting down why a balance moved: suspense, intercompany between sites and clearing accounts.

lenses.faster: Fixed checks (suspense zero, clearing accounts nil, intercompany balanced, movement above threshold) run on the AFAS trial balance; a model call lists likely causes per flagged account from the booking lines, cutting the review from a day to a few hours.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar triggers the checks on day one; flagged accounts come with a proposed cause, and the bookkeeper decides corrections.
lenses.ambitious: Run the same checks every week instead of monthly, so problems are fixed before close and days to close drops; demand grows because each early fix saves close time.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the Excel compare; bookkeepers want more time solving the real errors.
lenses.options: Little; the balance is a fact.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the check list and thresholds per account and decides which corrections they book directly; more expert in the ledger.
reach: Take over balance-sheet account reconciliations from the Accountants, learning reconciliation standards
Prepare intercompany site settlements with the Controller, learning intercompany rules

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a movement is a booking error or a real business change, and when to escalate to the Controller.
tasks.pattern_why: The checks can be written down per account and run without a model.

steps: Script pulls the AFAS trial balance
Rules flag suspense, clearing, intercompany and threshold movements
Model summarises booking lines behind each flag
Bookkeeper books or escalates corrections
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every correcting entry; Controller signs off the trial balance.
in_practice.logs_to: Close checklist in SharePoint with check results and corrections

evidence.claim: Rule-based trial-balance checks on ERP data are standard close practice.
Booking proposals alone do not automate; own accounts and exceptions per administration block touchless shares.

risks: Thresholds set too wide hide errors before the audit
Check list not updated when the chart of accounts changes
research_questions: How many audit adjustments last year traced back to balances the trial-balance review could have caught?
How long does the trial-balance step take in today's close?
Which accounts cause most month-end questions?

tasks.short: Pull actuals and last year's budget from AFAS into the budget template for each site and cost centre.

today.trigger: Annual budget cycle and quarterly re-forecast set by FP&A.
steps: Export actuals per cost centre from AFAS
Copy last year's budget into the FP&A template
Fill known contracts (rent, leases, agency fees)
Send sheets to cost-centre owners and collect replies
Hand the compiled file to FP&A
today.time_sinks: Merging versions from cost-centre owners and checking they did not break formulas.

lenses.faster: The template fills from AFAS actuals and contract data by script, owners enter numbers in one shared sheet, and checks flag gaps; compiling drops by about half.
lenses.autonomous: The FP&A cycle start fills sheets per cost centre and sends reminders; the bookkeeper handles gaps and the merged file goes to FP&A.
lenses.ambitious: Give each site's operations manager a monthly rolling view of flex-worker cost against budget for the first time; demand grows as it gets cheaper because flex spend swings with the season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging Excel versions; bookkeepers want to add what they know about contracts and supplier price rises.
lenses.options: Scenarios on flex-worker volume and agency rates change the budget decision; drafting two or three is now cheap.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper supplies the contract and supplier cost baseline and decides which known commitments go in; more involved in planning.
reach: Take over the baseline cost build from the FP&A Analysts, learning driver-based budgeting
Maintain the contract register with the Controller, learning contract terms

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier contracts end, renew or rise, which no export shows.
tasks.pattern_why: Filling a template from AFAS and contract data follows written rules; FP&A keeps the judgement.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A opens the budget or forecast cycle
steps: Script fills template from AFAS actuals and last budget
Known contract costs added from the contract register
Shared sheet sent to owners with reminders
Checks flag blanks and large changes for the bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: FP&A and the Finance Director approve the budget; the bookkeeper approves the baseline.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder with version history

evidence.claim: Template filling from ERP actuals and shared input sheets replaces manual merging in budget cycles.

risks: Owners rely on prefilled numbers and stop thinking about changes
research_questions: How many hours do the bookkeepers spend in the budget cycle, and on which steps?
Is there a contract register with end dates and indexation clauses?
Does FP&A want a fixed template or its own model?

tasks.short: Keep stock records of own pallets, packaging and fuel in line with counts and invoices in AFAS.

today.trigger: Monthly stock count from the sites and month close.
steps: Receive count sheets from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Compare counts with AFAS stock and purchases
Book differences and revalue stock
Ask sites about large differences
today.time_sinks: Late and inconsistent count sheets from three sites, and explaining pallet differences (exchange pallets).

lenses.faster: Sites enter counts in one form, the form posts to a comparison against AFAS, and only differences above a threshold need the bookkeeper; the monthly job shrinks by about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: The count form closing starts the comparison and a draft difference booking; the bookkeeper approves it.
lenses.ambitious: Track exchange-pallet balances per customer and carrier monthly for the first time, so Noordhaven can invoice missing pallets; demand grows because pallet loss is real money.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping count sheets; bookkeepers want to find where stock goes missing.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets difference thresholds and valuation rules and decides when a site must recount; slightly more expert.
reach: Take over pallet-balance statements with customers from the Credit and Collections Officer, learning pallet exchange agreements

tasks.human_edge: Talking to site staff about why counts differ and spotting when a difference hides loss or theft.
tasks.pattern_why: Count versus book comparison and valuation follow fixed rules.

steps: Form data compared to AFAS stock and receipts
Differences valued at the agreed price
Draft correcting entry prepared
Bookkeeper approves or asks site to recount
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves stock corrections; Controller above a set amount.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS memorial booking with attached count

evidence.claim: Structured count capture compared to ledger stock is standard practice and needs no model.

risks: Sites enter counts carelessly once the form is easy
Client-owned stock mixed with own stock
research_questions: Which stock does Noordhaven itself carry on the balance sheet, and how much is it worth?
How large are monthly pallet differences?
Do sites already count in a WMS that could feed AFAS directly?

tasks.short: Prepare VAT returns, ICP listings and statistics forms from AFAS and check agency g-rekening payments.

today.trigger: Monthly or quarterly VAT deadline, ICP deadline, CBS requests, and agency invoices that need the g-rekening split.
steps: Run VAT reports in AFAS
Check reverse-charge and intra-EU purchases by hand
Fill the return and ICP listing for the Controller to file
Check agency invoices for the g-rekening share and payment-behaviour statements
File proof in SharePoint
drudgery: Hand-checking VAT codes line by line
today.time_sinks: Finding wrong VAT codes and missing reverse-charge bookings before filing.

lenses.faster: Fixed checks flag VAT code against supplier country and type, reverse charge, and missing g-rekening splits; the return is prefilled and the bookkeeper reviews only flags, saving about a third.
lenses.autonomous: Each agency invoice is checked at receipt for the g-rekening share and a valid payment-behaviour statement; the VAT run is prepared on the deadline calendar and the Controller files.
lenses.ambitious: Check agency invoices against time records and split the g-rekening share on every invoice, so liability for the agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT is managed every week, not at audit.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses line-by-line VAT code checking; bookkeepers want to understand tax treatments better.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the VAT code rules and the agency-liability checklist; more expert in Dutch tax compliance.
reach: Take over VAT return preparation from the Accountant, learning VAT rules for logistics
Prepare for e-invoicing reporting with the Controller, learning Peppol and ViDA basics

tasks.human_edge: Judging unusual transactions for VAT and deciding when to ask the tax adviser; signing responsibility stays with people.
tasks.pattern_why: VAT code and g-rekening checks are written rules; no model needed.

in_practice.trigger: Tax deadline calendar; agency invoice received
steps: Rules check VAT codes and reverse charge on all purchase and sales lines
Agency invoices checked for g-rekening split and current payment-behaviour statement
Return and ICP prefilled from AFAS
Bookkeeper reviews flags, Controller files
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves and files every return; bookkeeper approves g-rekening splits in the payment run.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint tax folder with check results and filed returns

evidence.claim: Hirers can be liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and limit this with payment-behaviour statements, records and paying into the g-rekening.
Mandatory B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031 are planned but not yet law.
Under ViDA reporting, buyers may need to report intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases within 5 days of receipt.

risks: Rules miss a new transaction type and errors are filed
research_questions: What share of the three agencies' invoices is paid into the g-rekening today?
How many VAT corrections were needed in the past two years?
Who files returns today, and what does the external accountant check?

role.altitude: From keying, exporting and matching to owning AFAS match rules, tolerances, VAT code rules, supplier master data and the agency-liability checks, with a short exception queue each morning and more time on disputes, suppliers and close.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: daily paid/unpaid status and pallet balances
Accountant: balance-sheet reconciliations and VAT return preparation
FP&A Analyst: cost baselines and cost-per-shift comparisons
Payroll Specialist: checking agency rates against CAO pay tables
role.ceiling_note: Most of these tasks are small (20–40 hours per FTE a year); the big gains sit in invoice processing and bank matching. Limits are messy PDF and agency invoices, own VAT codes per administration, and that the Controller and Finance Director keep sign-off on returns and the trial balance.
skills_to_grow: AFAS Profit setup: match rules, tolerances, workflows
role.ambitious_version: The three bookkeepers run a weekly mini-close and a flex-worker cost service for the three sites: every agency invoice checked against time records with the g-rekening split, weekly trial-balance checks, and site managers seeing their own open items, cutting days to close.
